title: What is the first accumulation point of the scl spectrum in a free group?
body:
## The question

Let F be free and let scl(F) denote the set of values scl(g) for g a nontrivial
element (or more generally a chain) in F. The set is contained in the rationals,
and by the Duncan-Howie theorem it is bounded below by 1/2 on the commutator
subgroup.

What is the smallest accumulation point of scl(F)?

Equivalently: below which value is the spectrum discrete? The answer would say
where the combinatorially rigid bottom of the spectrum stops and the continuum-like
behaviour begins.
